content:
Aisha Bello: got paged 7 times overnight on audit exporter. all were basically the same thing: Splunk HEC 429s for a single beta tenant + pipeline lag staying > 30m while it caught up. can we tune alert thresholds + add a sane maintenance silence story before we burn out on this :/ 

Sean Gallagher: yeah saw those. looking at grafana it was never actually stuck, just throttled and then backfilled. we’re paging on `redwood_audit_exporter_pipeline_lag_seconds` which is customer-facing lag, not “we’re dead in the water”.

Rafael Mendes: +1. also a bunch of pages were during the scheduled backfill window we kicked off for Helio (they asked for 24h backfill). pipeline lag will scream no matter what.

Allison Grant: can we confirm the alert rules? i think the current page condition is:
- pipeline_lag > 30m for 15m (beta tenants)
that’s basically “page whenever downstream is slow”. too aggressive.

Caleb Johnson: yeah that’s what’s in the alertmanager config from pr-392. we *do* have processing lag metric available now:
- `redwood_audit_exporter_processing_lag_seconds` (now - last_polled_ts)
which is the “exporter isn’t making progress reading events” signal.

Logan Wright: re: 429s, exporter is doing what it should: backing off + reducing batch size + occasionally auto-pausing. if we page every time splunk rate limits, we’ll just be paging for customer-side capacity.

Aisha Bello: ok proposal:
1) PAGE off processing lag (stuck) not pipeline lag (catching up)
2) PIPELINE lag becomes ticket/customer-health surfacing
3) add a clean way to silence during planned backfills / customer maintenance

Sean Gallagher: aligned. suggest these changes (beta):
- PAGE: `processing_lag > 15m for 20m` for any beta tenant AND exporter not in `paused_reason=customer_requested` (or maintenance)
- PAGE: exporter `auto_paused == 1` for > 30m AND affects >= 2 beta tenants (systemic)
- TICKET: pipeline_lag > 60m for 60m (per tenant+dest) w/ annotation “likely downstream throttling or backfill; see runbook”

Rafael Mendes: make sure we still page if exporter is crashlooping / no heartbeats. that’s separate and should remain sensitive.

Sean Gallagher: yep keep:
- PAGE: exporter up==0 for 5m (service down)
- PAGE: queue depth growing + processing lag increasing (we’re accumulating)

Allison Grant: careful with “any beta tenant” + per-tenant labels, that’s still going to be noisy if a single customer is constantly throttling. can we set “any beta tenant” only for processing lag, but require >=2 tenants for retryable error rate / pause?

Aisha Bello: that works for me. the pages we got weren’t processing lag anyway, they were pipeline lag.

Caleb Johnson: implementation detail: we can change alert expressions to use `max_over_time(processing_lag[20m]) > 900` etc. and keep tenant label only for allowlisted. for “>=2 tenants”, we can `count by () (processing_lag > X)` style, but we need to ensure the metric includes tenant label consistently.

Logan Wright: metrics side, we already gate tenant labels to the beta allowlist. so counting impacted tenants should be stable for now.

Rafael Mendes: maintenance silences: what’s the expected workflow? we can’t have SREs manually crafting alertmanager silences every time CS schedules a backfill.

Aisha Bello: +1. we need something repeatable. even if it’s manual, it should be templated + documented.

Sean Gallagher: near-term (this week): add runbook section w/ “how to silence a destination during planned backfill / customer maintenance”:
- create alertmanager silence matching `tenant_id` + `destination_type` (or destination_id if we have it) for X hours
- include a standard reason string (“planned backfill for customer request”) and require an owner

Allison Grant: ok, but let’s also add guardrails: we should not silence exporter-down / processing lag globally. silence should only match pipeline-lag + adapter error tickets.

Caleb Johnson: we can split alerts into 2 groups:
- paging alerts (processing lag, service down, queue growth) in a “never silence broadly” group
- customer-facing alerts (pipeline lag, terminal 4xx, elevated retries) in a “silence allowed” group
then docs can point to the right ones.

Logan Wright: longer-term we could introduce a config-level “maintenance_mode” in control plane so exporter emits `maintenance=1` label and the alert rules exclude it. but that’s code + UX.

Rafael Mendes: i’d rather do it in product eventually. support will ask for it the second we onboard more beta customers.

Sean Gallagher: agree, but for beta we can start with alertmanager silences + a checklist. we can open a follow-up ticket for control-plane maintenance flag.

Aisha Bello: for “lag windows”: should we also widen the evaluation window? the 15m/15m was too twitchy.

Allison Grant: yes. recommend:
- processing lag: threshold 15m, `for: 20m` (so it’s truly stuck)
- pipeline lag ticket: threshold 60m, `for: 60m` (so we don’t spam tickets during normal catch-up)
- page on pipeline lag only if it’s extreme (e.g. > 6h) AND not in maintenance/backfill

Rafael Mendes: +1 on “extreme pipeline lag” as a page. if we’re 6h behind and no one notices, that’s bad even if it’s “downstream”.

Sean Gallagher: ok, add:
- PAGE: pipeline_lag > 6h for 30m AND processing_lag < 5m (meaning exporter is working but we’re not catching up fast enough)
This catches “customer sink permanently throttling us” scenarios where we need to intervene (pause, talk to customer, adjust batching).

Aisha Bello: nice. it also avoids paging during true stuckness (processing lag handles that).

Caleb Johnson: we should annotate alerts with links:
- grafana dashboard
- runbook section
- “how to silence” snippet

Logan Wright: +1. and we should add a panel on dashboard: “pages fired (last 24h)” + “silences active”.

Allison Grant: please also update the paging policy blurb: pages should be actionable. if the action is “wait for splunk to stop 429ing”, that’s not actionable at 2am.

Rafael Mendes: who’s taking the change? also we should do a 1-week lookback after we adjust and see if we’re missing real issues.

Sean Gallagher: i’ll patch the alert rules today + update the confluence SLO/alerting page with the new thresholds + silence process. Logan/Caleb can you sanity check the prometheus queries?

Caleb Johnson: yep, send the pr link.

Logan Wright: i’ll review for metric correctness + dashboards.

Aisha Bello: i’ll update the on-call runbook with the maintenance silence steps once Sean lands the new alert names/labels.

Rafael Mendes: please also add an “if pipeline lag ticket fires” section: check if backfill is running, check splunk 429s, confirm exporter not paused, decide whether to pause the destination and notify CS.

Sean Gallagher: ack. i’ll incorporate that into runbook notes.

Allison Grant: last thing: can we change the pager routing so audit-exporter pages go to SRE-primary but also drop a slack msg to #eng-security-beta (or whatever) during beta? product/CS tends to ask “are we down?” and we end up relaying manually.

Aisha Bello: good call. maybe just a slack notification for P1/P2 alerts.

Sean Gallagher: i can add a slack receiver for the paging alerts only (not tickets), to #eng-sre and #customer-success? (or at least #eng-sre + tag Miguel when it’s a beta tenant)

Rafael Mendes: let’s keep it to #eng-sre for now; CS noise will be a lot. but we can add an annotation field that includes “beta_tenant=true” + tenant name so we can loop in CSM when needed.

Sean Gallagher: sounds good. i’ll proceed:
- change page signals to processing lag + extreme pipeline lag
- widen windows
- document silences + maintenance/backfill guidelines
will post PR + updated doc link here.

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup: thanks. would love to stop waking up to “lag 31m” pages.

Caleb Johnson: same. ping when PR is up.

Logan Wright: +1, will review quickly once it’s posted.
